page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

This server includes 3780 GB of local NVMe storage and is Premium Storage capable, making it suitable for workloads requiring high-speed local disk access. It does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in several areas. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2110.0 and a multi-core score of 16603.0, both categorized in the top 25%. It also demonstrated strong results in image processing (16090.0), text processing (2656.0), and the Passmark CPU physics test (7137.8). For small-scale language model tasks, it achieved a strong text generation speed of 296.69 tokens per second using a 135M parameter model. However, memory performance was relatively weak, with a Passmark memory score of 1572.37 placing it in the bottom 25%. Large-scale LLM inference using a 70B model was poor, yielding only 2.45 tokens per second.

Given its high memory capacity of 512.0 GB and 3780 GB of local storage, this server offers high resource density for memory-intensive applications. It is well-suited for large databases, memory-cached applications, enterprise resource planning systems, and data processing pipelines. The inclusion of Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that can leverage hardware-accelerated vector and matrix mathematics without requiring dedicated GPU resources.
